name: Wisetack
headline: Wisetack financing for mid-size solar and home-service jobs
summary: Wisetack focuses on smaller to mid-sized residential projects with loan originations capped at $25,000 — a fit for repairs, inverter swaps, battery retrofits, and HVAC more than whole-home solar-plus-storage — delivered through conversion-optimized embeddable widgets.

key_facts.label: Best fit
key_facts.value: Repairs, inverter replacements, battery retrofits, HVAC

key_facts.label: Integration speed
key_facts.value: Partners often go live in about three weeks

key_facts.label: Auth
key_facts.value: OAuth 2.0 Bearer tokens; REST (+ GraphQL in some partners)

sections.heading: Where Wisetack sits in the stack
sections.body: Unlike tier-one solar lenders optimized for $30k–$100k+ EPCs, Wisetack’s hard cap makes it a specialist rail for ancillary and mid-ticket work. That can be a feature: faster embeds, clearer consumer UX, and webhook-driven ops without enterprise API programs.

sections.heading: Widget suite built for conversion
sections.body: Rather than forcing every partner to build UI from scratch, Wisetack provides embeddable components: slide-to-estimate calculators for term/payment exploration, monthly payment microcopy (“As low as $/mo”) fed by pricing GET endpoints, and a soft-pull Prequalify Path via redirect or modal CTA.

table.caption: Wisetack widget types
rows: Adjust terms (e.g. 12–60 months) and see estimated payments
iframe or JS snippet synced to project total
Dynamic “As low as $/mo” on estimates and invoices
GET pricing endpoint with invoice total
Soft-pull decision in minutes without score impact
Redirect or modal from primary CTA

sections.heading: Webhooks that drive the CRM
sections.body: When funding clears, Wisetack can POST state changes that automatically move a job to “Contract Signed,” trigger homeowner welcome sequences, and notify procurement to order modules or inverters. That event-driven design is the operational reason mid-market shops adopt the platform quickly.

sections.heading: Homeowner checklist for Wisetack offers
sections.body: Confirm the financed amount is within product limits, understand whether your job is repair vs full system, and still get a cash price. A widget payment estimate is not a substitute for the final TILA disclosures.

questions_to_ask: Is my project under the $25k cap after change orders?
Was this a soft-pull prequal or a final application?
What APR/term options were returned, and can I see them in writing?
red_flags: Using Wisetack-sized financing language on a whole-home solar + battery package that will exceed $25k.
Only widget marketing copy — no final loan agreement provided before work starts.

faqs.question: Can Wisetack finance my entire new rooftop solar system?
faqs.answer: Often no — the $25k cap blocks many full installs. It is better matched to repairs, equipment swaps, and mid-size add-ons. Ask about GoodLeap, Sunlight, Hearth, or cash/HELOC alternatives for larger scopes.

faqs.question: Does the prequalify path hurt my credit?
faqs.answer: Wisetack markets a soft-pull pre-qualification that does not impact credit score the way a hard inquiry does. Confirm on the disclosure screen before submitting.
